NDT software in Houston: what local inspection companies actually need

NDT software for a Houston company has to handle more variety than almost anywhere else in North America. One Houston inspection company might have a UT thickness crew on the Houston Ship Channel on Monday, a radiography crew shooting pipeline tie-ins north of the city on Tuesday, and a PAUT technician in a fabrication shop in northwest Houston all week. The Atlantis ERP solution is built for that mix. Technician certifications, instrument calibration, dispatch, reports, quotes and invoices sit in one system, set up for your company instead of patched together from spreadsheets.

The local market sets the requirements. The Ship Channel corridor, running from the Port of Houston out towards Baytown, has one of the largest groups of refineries and petrochemical plants in the world. The Energy Corridor and downtown hold the headquarters of the operators, pipeline companies and EPC contractors who write the inspection specifications. Around them sit hundreds of fabrication shops, heat exchanger shops, valve shops and tank builders, all buying NDT. OSHA's process safety management standard puts mechanical integrity at the centre of every plant's programme, TCEQ watches emissions events closely, and PHMSA regulates the interstate pipelines that run out of the city. For an NDT contractor, that means clients who audit your paperwork as closely as your technique.

The Houston contractors we talk to range from a handful of technicians to a few hundred. Most have a core of full-time Level IIs and a bench of travelling techs they bring in for the spring and fall turnaround seasons. Hurricane season runs from June through November and adds more pressure: schedules move at short notice and crews have to be moved quickly.

ERP for NDT companies in Houston: one system instead of five

An ERP for NDT companies in Houston should replace the certification spreadsheet, the calibration binder, the whiteboard dispatch board, the report templates on a shared drive and the separate accounting package. The Atlantis ERP brings all of these into one database, so a technician, an instrument, a job and an invoice all point at the same records.

In practice most Houston shops run something like this: certifications live in Excel, calibration certificates sit in a filing cabinet or an email folder, the operations manager dispatches from memory and a whiteboard, reports come from Word templates, and billing runs on a separate accounting package fed by paper timesheets. Every handoff between those tools is a chance for a mistake. An expired UT cert slips through, a gauge goes out overdue for calibration, or a day of standby never gets billed.

With the Atlantis ERP, the job created from an accepted quotation carries the client PO, site, methods, codes and acceptance criteria. The team assignment on that job checks technician availability and blocks double-booking. Timesheets logged against the job warn when a technician's certificate is not valid, and the hours flow into the invoice with labour, equipment and consumables subtotals. See the full list of apps at Atlantis ERP apps.

Technician certification tracking for Houston refinery turnarounds

Technician certification tracking software for Houston turnarounds has to answer one question fast: is every tech on this crew certified, in date and vision-tested for the methods they will perform on this site? The Certificates app records scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT and training hours, and attachments for each technician.

Status is calculated automatically as active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked, and there are dedicated Expiring Soon and Expired menus. Vision tests are tracked separately, covering near vision at Jaeger J1 or J2, far vision, colour perception, contrast, the examiner and clinic, with their own expiry. Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before a cert or vision test lapses, and configurable email alerts go to whoever you choose.

This matters in Houston because turnaround crews are assembled fast. When a refinery on the Ship Channel pulls a unit down in March, you may be adding travelling techs from Louisiana, Oklahoma or out of state within a week. Their certs, vision tests and written practice evidence need to be entered, checked and printable before badging. The employee NDT profile also stores highest level, methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, so one record answers the client's pre-mobilisation document request.

Crew dispatch software for Ship Channel plants, pipelines and shops

Crew dispatch software for a Houston NDT company needs to stop double-booking and show who is free next. The Team Assignments app runs each job through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed, with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates.

The technician availability calendar holds assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable days, and overlaps are blocked. A technician cannot be put on two jobs at once, and the same instrument serial number cannot be issued to two crews. If you try to send a flaw detector that is out of calibration, the system warns you. Each technician shows current assignment, utilisation and next available date, in calendar, kanban and list views.

Houston dispatch is complicated by distance and access. A crew heading to a Pasadena or Deer Park plant needs site orientation and permits; a crew heading up a pipeline right-of-way towards Conroe needs a different truck and a different kit. The project record carries safety induction and work permit fields, so the dispatcher can see what a site requires before crew names go on the job. When a storm forces a plant to shut down, you can see immediately which techs and which instruments are tied up, and where they can go instead.

Calibration management software for Houston instrument fleets

Calibration management software is where many Houston NDT companies fail audits. The Asset Management app tracks every flaw detector, thickness gauge, PAUT unit, probe, yoke and survey meter by serial number, with type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle status: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed.

Calibration records hold provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, whether the lab is accredited, pass, fail or conditional result and next due date. The calibration certificate register stores the lab accreditation number, the PDF and a valid, expiring or expired status, with expiry alerts. Issue and return goes through supervisor and manager approval, and condition is recorded both ways, which settles arguments about who dropped the probe.

Houston companies often rent instruments to other contractors or rent them in during a turnaround peak. Rental rates can be recorded against the asset, reservations prevent clashes, and inbound and outbound movements are logged. Consumables such as couplant, penetrant, developer, magnetic particle bath and PPE carry reorder levels and low-stock flags, which helps in the week before a big outage when everyone orders at once.

NDT reporting software for Houston refinery, pipeline and fabrication work

NDT reporting software for Houston has to cover every method the market buys. The NDT Reports app supports 17 report types: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday and coating, and computed radiography, each with its own numbering sequence.

Method-specific data is built in: UT probe calibration tables, RT source, technique and IQI type and placement, MT technique and particle type, PT method and developer, PAUT focal laws, and UT thickness readings by direction. Weld and job lines carry defect type and orientation, and every report ends with acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks. Reports move from draft to in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures plus a third-party or authorized inspector name and signature where the client requires it.

Houston operators and EPCs usually insist on their own report formats. Versioned company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML can be set up, and Excel templates are filled automatically by mapping fields to cells. Techs in the field use the offline app, which works without signal inside a plant, stores drafts and photos locally, captures signatures and syncs later. For clients who want to see results on a 3D model, reports can feed Digital Twin Reporting.

Industrial radiography in Houston: sources, vehicles and badges

Houston has a large industrial radiography workforce, and Texas regulates it through the Department of State Health Services radiation control programme. The ERP does not replace your radiation safety programme, but it keeps the records your RSO needs in one place.

The Fleet app marks which vehicles can carry radioactive sources and stores the transport licence number and expiry, along with vehicle assignment to a project and driver, with dates and mileage. The employee NDT profile holds radiation safety training and radiation badge number. RT reports capture source, technique and IQI details, and computed radiography has its own report type.

For night-shift shooting on a Ship Channel unit, the dispatcher can see which radiographers are current, which trucks are licensed for source transport and which survey meters are in calibration before the crew leaves the yard. Survey meters and other radiation instruments are tracked in Asset Management like any other instrument, with calibration due dates and alerts.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Houston operators and EPCs

NDT quoting and invoicing software should make it quick to quote a turnaround package and easy to bill it accurately afterwards. The Quotations app records job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with NDT service products flagged by method and category, a global discount, a branded quotation PDF, and online acceptance and signature that converts the quote to a sales order.

On the billing side, the Invoicing app puts the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector on the header, and shows labour, equipment and consumables subtotals. Lines carry cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby or setup), billable flag and rate multiplier, so overtime and standby actually reach the invoice.

Many Houston operators pay through their own procurement portals and want invoices that match PO lines exactly. A custom invoice layout is set up during implementation. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA and outstanding invoices over twelve months, which tells you whether that turnaround actually made money.

Inspection management software for Houston: procedures, NCRs and audits

Inspection management software for Houston companies also has to hold the written procedures that clients audit. The Procedures app keeps a register with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and the procedure text or file.

Procedures move through draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states, prepared, reviewed and approved by fields and dates, and locked approved revisions. Every revision is kept as a snapshot. An AI-assisted first draft can speed up writing a new procedure, but your Level III still reviews and approves it. Approvers get email notifications and reminders.

NCR and CAPA workflows can be configured during implementation, so a rejected weld or a client audit finding becomes a tracked action with an owner and a due date. Company certifications such as ISO accreditations are recorded with alert days, so the certificate you send with a prequalification package is never out of date.

Affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Houston: implementation

An affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Houston is one that is set up around your methods, your clients and your paperwork, without a long consulting project. Atlantis NDT is run by an ASNT NDT Level III, so implementation starts from how an NDT company actually works.

  • Discovery: we review your methods, report formats, certification scheme and client requirements, including any operator-specific templates.
  • Data load: technicians, certs, vision tests, instruments, calibration certificates, clients and open jobs are imported from your spreadsheets.
  • Templates: your report, quotation and invoice layouts are built with your logo and headers.
  • Integrations: the open REST API can connect to SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.
  • Training: office staff, dispatchers and field techs are trained on the parts they use.

Timing is planned around your season. Most Houston companies prefer to go live outside the spring and fall turnaround peaks. Pricing is a quote on request, sized to your company. Book a Houston NDT ERP demo to see it with your own methods.

The best NDT software is the one that covers certifications, calibration, dispatch, reports and billing in one place for your methods. The Atlantis ERP is built specifically for NDT companies and is configured for each client's workflows and report formats.

Does the Atlantis ERP work for small NDT companies in Houston?

Yes. It is designed to be affordable and accessible for small NDT companies as well as larger contractors. You use the apps you need, and pricing is a quote on request.

Can it track ISO 9712, PCN or CSWIP certificates as well as SNT-TC-1A?

Yes. Technician certificates can be recorded under SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other schemes, with level, method, dates and attachments.
